modelEssay.title: Wealth of the Mind is the Only True Wealth
modelEssay.content:
Wealth of the mind is often regarded as the only true wealth, a saying that emphasizes the value of knowledge and wisdom over material possessions. This belief is rooted in the idea that while physical wealth can be lost or depleted, the wealth of the mind is enduring and can be a source of infinite possibilities.

In today's fast-paced world, the importance of mental wealth is more evident than ever. Individuals who possess a wealth of knowledge are better equipped to adapt to changes and challenges. They can think critically, solve problems creatively, and contribute to society in meaningful ways. Moreover, mental wealth fosters personal growth and satisfaction, as it allows individuals to pursue their passions and achieve a sense of fulfillment that material wealth cannot provide.

In conclusion, the wealth of the mind is indeed the only true wealth because it is the foundation of personal and societal progress. It is the key to unlocking our potential and leads to a life of true richness and purpose.

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话一。

transcript.text: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您是牛津大学的物理学教授。

transcript.text: You're a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您是欧洲核子研究组织的高级顾问。

transcript.text: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您似乎还不知疲倦地环游世界，发表演讲。

transcript.text: And, in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 此外，您还有一个每周的科学电视节目。

transcript.text: Where do you get the energy?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您哪里来的精力？

transcript.text: Oh, well, I just love what I do.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 哦，嗯，我只是热爱我的工作。

transcript.text: I'm extremely fortunate to have this life, doing what I love doing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我非常幸运能过上这样的生活，做我热爱的事情。

transcript.text: Professor, what exactly is your goal?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 教授，您的目标到底是什么？

transcript.text: Why do you do all of this?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 您为什么做所有这些？

transcript.text: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on, but these, I think, can be divided into two groups, the education of science and the further understanding of science.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，正如您所说，我确实有各种不同的事情在进行，但我认为这些可以分为两类：科学教育和对科学的进一步理解。

transcript.text: Don't these two things get in the way of each other?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这两件事不会相互妨碍吗？

transcript.text: What I mean is, doesn't giving lectures take time away from the lab?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我的意思是，发表演讲不会占用实验室的时间吗？

transcript.text: Not really, no.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不完全是，不会。

transcript.text: I love teaching, and I don't mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我热爱教学，而且我不介意现在比过去花更多时间在教学上。

transcript.text: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 此外，我想说的是，教授一门学科有助于我更好地理解它。

transcript.text: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我发现，当我必须清楚地解释某事、帮助他人理解它以及回答关于它的问题时，这促进了我自己的知识。

transcript.text: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 无论一个人在所教授领域已有多少专业知识，高水平的教学对任何人来说都是非常有激励性的。

transcript.text: Of any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon, a significant discovery or invention we can expect soon.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 关于您预见在不久的将来会出现的任何科学突破，一个重要的发现或发明我们可以期待很快出现。

transcript.text: The world is always conducting science, and there are constantly new things being discovered.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 世界一直在进行科学研究，不断有新事物被发现。

transcript.text: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 事实上，现在我们有太多数据存放在计算机中。

transcript.text: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 例如，我们有数千张由望远镜拍摄的火星照片，但从未有人看过。

transcript.text: We have them, but nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们拥有这些照片，但没有人有时间亲眼查看它们，更不用说分析了。

options.label: C
options.text: By building upon previous discoveries.

transcript.text: Conversation two
transcript.translation: 对话二

transcript.text: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你认为梦有特殊含义吗？

transcript.text: No, I don't think they do.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不，我认为没有。

transcript.text: I don't either, but some people do.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我也不认为，但有些人这么认为。

transcript.text: I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我认为那些相信梦有特殊含义的人是迷信的，尤其是在当今。

transcript.text: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在过去，古埃及、古希腊或古中国时期，人们常常相信梦能预见未来。

transcript.text: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但今天，随着我们拥有的所有科学知识，我认为很难再相信这类事情了。

transcript.text: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我的祖母是迷信的，她认为梦能预测未来。

transcript.text: Once, she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有一次，她梦到她第二天要乘坐的航班坠毁了。

transcript.text: Can you guess what she did?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你能猜到她做了什么吗？

transcript.text: She didn't take that flight.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 她没有乘坐那个航班。

transcript.text: She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 她甚至第二天都没有去机场。

transcript.text: Instead, she took the same flight, but a week later.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 相反，她乘坐了同一个航班，但是一周后。

transcript.text: And everything was fine, of course.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当然，一切都没事。

transcript.text: No plane ever crashed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没有任何飞机坠毁。

transcript.text: How funny.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 真有趣。

transcript.text: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你知道吗，飞行实际上比其他任何交通方式都安全？

transcript.text: It's been statistically proven.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这已被统计证明。

transcript.text: People can be so irrational sometimes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们有时会如此非理性。

transcript.text: Yes, absolutely.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，绝对是。

transcript.text: But even if we think they're ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但即使我们认为它们荒谬，情感可能和理性思维一样强大。

transcript.text: Exactly.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 正是如此。

transcript.text: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们会因为他们的非理性感受而做出各种疯狂的事情。

transcript.text: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但事实上，一些心理学家认为，我们的梦是当天情感和记忆的结果。

transcript.text: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wish would happen.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我想是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说过，儿童的梦通常是他们愿望的简单表现，即他们希望发生的事情。

transcript.text: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但在成年人中，梦是他们更复杂情感的反映。

transcript.text: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand, using the scientific method, something as bizarre as dreams?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 心理学家试图用科学方法理解像梦这样奇异的东西，这难道不有趣吗？

transcript.text: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 心理学就像是对非理性感受的理性研究。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack.
transcript.translation: 当一些科学家探索南极洲表面时，另一些科学家正在深入了解冰层下四公里处的一个巨大水体。

transcript.text: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
transcript.translation: 科学家们在20世纪70年代首次通过使用穿透冰层的无线电波发现了沃斯托克湖。

transcript.text: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
transcript.translation: 自那以后，他们使用声波甚至卫星来绘制这个巨大水体的地图。

transcript.text: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
transcript.translation: 沃斯托克湖的水是如何在冰盖下保持液态的？

transcript.text: The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing, says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
transcript.translation: 威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说，上方厚实的冰川像隔热毯一样，防止水结冰。

transcript.text: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake.
transcript.translation: 此外，来自地球深处的地热可能温暖了这个隐藏的湖泊。

transcript.text: The scientists suspect that microorganisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than two million years.
transcript.translation: 科学家们怀疑，可能有微生物生活在沃斯托克湖中，这些微生物已与外界隔绝超过两百万年。

transcript.text: Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth, says Siegert.
transcript.translation: 西格特说，在那里发现的任何东西都将与地球表面的东西完全不同。

transcript.text: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
transcript.translation: 科学家们正在努力找到一种方法，钻入冰层并提取水样，而不造成污染。

transcript.text: Again, robots might be the solution.
transcript.translation: 同样，机器人可能是解决方案。

transcript.text: If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will melt through the surface ice.
transcript.translation: 如果一切按计划进行，一个钻头形状的机器人将融化穿透表面冰层。

transcript.text: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
transcript.translation: 当它到达湖泊时，它将释放另一个机器人，该机器人可以在湖中游泳、拍照并寻找生命迹象。

transcript.text: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and arid conditions.
transcript.translation: 科学家们希望他们的发现能揭示外太空生命，这些生命可能存在于类似的黑暗和干旱条件中。

transcript.text: Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter's moon Europa showed signs of water beneath its icy surface.
transcript.translation: 最近，木星卫星欧罗巴的近距离图片显示了其冰层下有水的迹象。

transcript.text: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there, too.
transcript.translation: 一旦在南极洲测试过，机器人也可以被派往欧罗巴去寻找那里的生命。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984 when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
transcript.translation: 1984年，詹姆斯·科普兰产生了研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人的想法，当时他发现关于他们的语言研究很少。

transcript.text: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
transcript.translation: 他通过一位在墨西哥与部落成员合作的社会工作者联系到了一位部落成员。

transcript.text: At first, the tribe member, named Gonzales, was very reluctant to cooperate.
transcript.translation: 起初，这位名叫冈萨雷斯的部落成员非常不愿意合作。

transcript.text: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language.
transcript.translation: 他告诉科普兰，再多的钱也买不到他的语言。

transcript.text: But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research, and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzales agreed to help.
transcript.translation: 但在科普兰向他解释了他的研究意图，以及这将如何使塔拉乌马拉人受益后，冈萨雷斯同意帮忙。

transcript.text: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
transcript.translation: 他带科普兰去了他的村庄，并担任了中间人。

transcript.text: Copeland says, thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us.
transcript.translation: 科普兰说，多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人明白了我们的使命，并开始信任我们。

transcript.text: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
transcript.translation: 进入塔拉乌马拉人的世界对科普兰来说是一个艰巨的项目。

transcript.text: To reach their homeland, he must drive two and a half days from Houston, Texas.
transcript.translation: 要到达他们的家园，他必须从得克萨斯州休斯顿开车两天半。

transcript.text: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get, and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
transcript.translation: 他装满车辆，带上部落成员不易获得的物品，并将这些物品作为友谊的象征送给他们。

transcript.text: The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
transcript.translation: 塔拉乌马拉人不相信积累财富，他们接收食物并互相分享。

transcript.text: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, it also has enriched his life in several ways.
transcript.translation: 对科普兰来说，这次经历不仅在学术上令人满意，还在多个方面丰富了他的生活。

transcript.text: I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the tradition, he says.
transcript.translation: 他说：“我看到人们拒绝技术，过着非常艰苦的传统生活，这让我对传统中进步的意义有了另一种理解。”

transcript.text: I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
transcript.translation: 我体验了在自然中生活的简单，否则我只能从书本上读到。

transcript.text: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other.
transcript.translation: 我在他们的分享意识和相互关怀中看到了很多美好。

transcript.text: What is a radical?
transcript.translation: 什么是激进分子？

transcript.text: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them.
transcript.translation: 如今人们似乎对这个词感到恐惧，尤其是害怕被贴上这个标签。

transcript.text: Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white male in Western society.
transcript.translation: 指控个人或团体激进通常是为了迫使他们沉默屈服，从而维持现状，更重要的是，保护西方社会中少数富裕白人男性的权力。

transcript.text: Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
transcript.translation: 女权主义是这一现象的绝佳例证。

transcript.text: The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism, when the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
transcript.translation: 妇女运动一直受到刻板印象、媒体的错误描绘以及仇视男性和激进主义的指控所困扰，而女权主义的基本基础仅仅是女性在生活的所有方面应享有平等权利。

transcript.text: When faced with the threat of being labeled radical, women back down from their worthy cause and consequently participate in their own oppression.
transcript.translation: 当面临被贴上激进标签的威胁时，女性从她们有价值的事业中退缩，从而参与了对自身的压迫。

transcript.text: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word.
transcript.translation: 已经到了这样一个地步，许多女性因为这个词所带的污名而不敢自称女权主义者。

transcript.text: If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
transcript.translation: 如果人们拒绝被污名所控制和恐吓，污名就会失去所有力量。

transcript.text: Without fear on which to feed, such stigmas can only die.
transcript.translation: 没有恐惧可以滋养，这样的污名只能消亡。

transcript.text: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
transcript.translation: 在我看来，激进分子就是反抗规范或倡导改变现状的人。

transcript.text: On closer inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
transcript.translation: 仔细观察就会发现，规范是不断演变的，因此不是固定不变的实体。

transcript.text: So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation?
transcript.translation: 那么，为什么偏离现状如此具有威胁性，而现状本身却不稳定且不断变化呢？

transcript.text: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the rise of those who don't.
transcript.translation: 这一切都归结于维护掌权者的权力并防止无权者崛起。

transcript.text: In fact, when we look at the word radical in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
transcript.translation: 事实上，当我们从历史背景来看“激进”这个词时，我们现在推崇为英雄的几乎每一个人在他或她的时代都被视为激进分子。

transcript.text: Radicals are people who affect change.
transcript.translation: 激进分子是影响变革的人。

transcript.text: They are the people about whom history is written.
transcript.translation: 他们是历史记载的人物。

transcript.text: Abolitionists were radicals.
transcript.translation: 废奴主义者是激进分子。

transcript.text: Civil rights activists were radicals.
transcript.translation: 民权活动家是激进分子。

transcript.text: Even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
transcript.translation: 甚至我们国家的创始人为赢得从英国的独立而战时也是激进分子。

transcript.text: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
transcript.translation: 他们在历史上的存在改变了我们社会的运作方式，主要是通过改变先前存在的权力平衡。

transcript.text: Of course, there are some radicals who've made a negative impact on humanity, but undeniably there would simply be no progress without radicals.
transcript.translation: 当然，有些激进分子对人类产生了负面影响，但不可否认的是，没有激进分子就根本没有进步。

transcript.text: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
transcript.translation: 话虽如此，下次有人称我为激进分子时，我将自豪地接受这个标签。

transcript.text: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
transcript.translation: 我们非常容易受到周围人的影响。

transcript.text: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so and has returned with an accent perhaps.
transcript.translation: 例如，你可能认识某人，他出国一年左右，回来后可能带点口音。

transcript.text: We become part of our immediate environment.
transcript.translation: 我们成为我们直接环境的一部分。

transcript.text: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world and let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
transcript.translation: 我们中没有人能免疫自己世界的影响，别自欺欺人地认为我们不受生活中事物和人的影响。

transcript.text: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory.
transcript.translation: Fred去工厂开始他的新工作。

transcript.text: Fred takes a 10-minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
transcript.translation: Fred休息10分钟喝咖啡，但其他工人休息半小时。

transcript.text: Fred says, what's the matter with you guys?
transcript.translation: Fred说，你们怎么了？

transcript.text: Weeks later, Fred is taking 20-minute breaks.
transcript.translation: 几周后，Fred休息20分钟。

transcript.text: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
transcript.translation: 一个月后，Fred也休息半小时。

transcript.text: Fred is saying, if you can't beat them, join them.
transcript.translation: Fred说，如果打不过他们，就加入他们。

transcript.text: Why would I work any harder than the next guy?
transcript.translation: 我为什么要比别人更努力工作？

transcript.text: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
transcript.translation: 关于为人最有趣的是，通常我们没有意识到心态正在发生变化。

transcript.text: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air.
transcript.translation: 这就像在新鲜空气里待了几周后回到城市烟雾中一样。

transcript.text: Only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells.
transcript.translation: 直到那时我们才意识到自己已经习惯了那些难闻的气味。

transcript.text: Mix with critical people and we learn to criticize.
transcript.translation: 与挑剔的人交往，我们就学会批评。

transcript.text: Mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
transcript.translation: 与快乐的人交往，我们就学会快乐。

transcript.text: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
transcript.translation: 这意味着我们需要决定从生活中想要什么，然后相应地选择我们的同伴。

transcript.text: You may well say, that is going to take some effort.
transcript.translation: 你可能会说，这需要一些努力。

transcript.text: It may not be comfortable.
transcript.translation: 可能不会很舒适。

transcript.text: I may offend some of my present company.
transcript.translation: 我可能会冒犯我现在的一些同伴。

transcript.text: Right, but it is your life.
transcript.translation: 没错，但这是你的生活。

transcript.text: Fred may say, I'm always broke, frequently depressed, I'm going nowhere, and I never do anything exciting.
transcript.translation: Fred可能会说，我总是破产，经常沮丧，一事无成，从不做任何令人兴奋的事。

transcript.text: Then we discover that Fred's best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere, and wishing that life was more exciting.
transcript.translation: 然后我们发现Fred的最好朋友也总是破产，经常沮丧，一事无成，并希望生活更刺激。

transcript.text: This is not coincidence, nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
transcript.translation: 这不是巧合，我们也无权评判Fred。

transcript.text: However, if Fred wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he'll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years.
transcript.translation: 然而，如果Fred想改善生活质量，他首先需要认识到这些年到底发生了什么。

transcript.text: It's no surprise that doctors, as a profession, suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
transcript.translation: 医生这个职业身体健康问题多不足为奇，因为他们一生都与病人打交道。

transcript.text: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
transcript.translation: 由于相关原因，精神科医生职业中的自杀率较高。

transcript.text: Traditionally, nine out of ten children whose parents smoke, smoke themselves.
transcript.translation: 传统上，父母吸烟的孩子中，十个有九个自己也吸烟。

transcript.text: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
transcript.translation: 肥胖部分是一个环境问题。

transcript.text: Successful people are successful friends and so the story goes on.
transcript.translation: 成功的人有成功的朋友，如此循环往复。

transcript.text: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
transcript.translation: 几乎每个美国人只需一眼就能认出美元钞票。

transcript.text: Many can identify it by its sound or texture, but few people indeed can accurately describe the world's most powerful important currency.
transcript.translation: 许多人能通过声音或质地识别它，但确实很少有人能准确描述世界上最强大、最重要的货币。

transcript.text: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other.
transcript.translation: 美国美元钞票一面用黑色墨水印刷，另一面用绿色墨水印刷。

transcript.text: The exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
transcript.translation: 纸张和墨水的确切成分是政府严密保守的秘密。

transcript.text: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
transcript.translation: 尽管它非常重要，但美元钞票实际上很轻。

transcript.text: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
transcript.translation: 需要近500张钞票才能使天平达到一磅的重量。

transcript.text: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief lifespan.
transcript.translation: 美元钞票不仅轻便，而且寿命短暂。

transcript.text: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
transcript.translation: 很少有美元钞票能存活超过18个月。

transcript.text: The word dollar is taken from the German word Tala, the name for the world's most important currency in the 16th century.
transcript.translation: 美元一词源自德语单词Tala，这是16世纪世界上最重要货币的名称。

transcript.text: The Tala was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany.
transcript.translation: Tala是一种银币，于1518年在德国皇帝查理五世统治时期首次铸造。

transcript.text: The concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
transcript.translation: 纸币的概念在美国货币史上是一个相对较新的创新。

transcript.text: When the constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
transcript.translation: 当宪法签署时，由于纸币在殖民时代价值持续下降，人们对纸币评价不高。

transcript.text: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted many coins for common currency.
transcript.translation: 由于这种缺乏信任，新美国政府铸造了许多硬币作为通用货币。

transcript.text: Interest-bearing banknotes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
transcript.translation: 同时发行了带利息的钞票，但其目的仅限于为紧急政府危机提供资金，例如美国参与1812年战争。

transcript.text: The first non-interest-bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862 at the height of the Civil War.
transcript.translation: 第一张无息纸币于1862年美国内战最激烈时由国会授权发行。

transcript.text: At this point, citizens' old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
transcript.translation: 此时，公民对贬值纸币的旧有恐惧已经平息，美元钞票由此诞生。

transcript.text: The new green-colored paper money quickly earned the name greenback.
transcript.translation: 新的绿色纸币很快获得了“绿背钞票”的名称。

transcript.text: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve and is issued from the twelve Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
transcript.translation: 如今，美国美元钞票是美联储的产物，由美国各地的十二家联邦储备银行发行。

transcript.text: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately two billion bills in circulation at all times.
transcript.translation: 政府始终维持约二十亿张钞票的稳定流通供应。

transcript.text: Controversy continues to surround the true value of the dollar bill.
transcript.translation: 围绕美元钞票的真实价值的争议持续存在。

transcript.text: American history has seen generations of politicians argue in favor of a gold standard for American currency.
transcript.translation: 美国历史上，几代政治家都主张为美国货币实行金本位制。

transcript.text: However, for the present, the American dollar bill holds the value that is printed on it, and little more.
transcript.translation: 然而，目前，美国美元钞票仅保有其上面印刷的价值，除此之外几乎没有更多价值。

transcript.text: The only other guarantee on the bill is a Federal Reserve pledge as a confirmation in the form of government securities.
transcript.translation: 钞票上唯一的其他担保是美联储以政府证券形式提供的承诺确认。

questionGroups.title: Section A

paragraphs.text: It was perhaps when my parents—who also happen to be my housemates — left to go travelling for a couple of months recently that it __26__ on me why I had not yet left the family home.
paragraphs.translation: 或许是在最近我的父母——他们碰巧也是我的室友——离开去旅行几个月的时候，我才突然明白为什么我还没有离开家。

paragraphs.text: It wasn't that I relied on them for __27__ reasons, or to keep my life in order, or to ease the chaos of the home. These days, I rely on them for their company.
paragraphs.translation: 并不是因为我依赖他们处理后勤事务，或者维持生活的秩序，或者减轻家里的混乱。如今，我依赖他们是因为他们的陪伴。

paragraphs.text: I missed coming home and talking about my day at work, and I missed being able to read their faces and sense how their day was. I missed having unique __28__ into tiny details that make a life.
paragraphs.translation: 我怀念回家后谈论我一天的工作，怀念能够读懂他们的表情并感受他们一天过得如何。我怀念能对构成生活的微小细节有独特的洞察。

paragraphs.text: While the conversation about young adults staying longer at home is __29__ by talk of laziness, of dependence, of an inability for young people to pull themselves together, __30__ do we talk of the way, in my case at least, my relationship with my parents has __31__ strengthened the longer we have lived together.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然关于年轻人在家待更久的讨论很少涉及懒惰、依赖或年轻人无法振作自己，但刻板印象确实存在，至少在我的情况下，与父母生活在一起的时间越长，我们的关系无疑就越牢固。

paragraphs.text: Over the years the power dynamic has changed and is no longer defined by one being the giver and another, the taker. So, what does this say for our relationships within the family home?
paragraphs.translation: 多年来，权力动态已经改变，不再由一方是给予者、另一方是接受者来定义。那么，这对我们家庭内部的关系意味着什么？

paragraphs.text: According to psychologist Sabina Read, there are "some very positive possible __32__ when adult children share the family home", noting the "parent-child relationship may indeed strengthen and mature" in the process.
paragraphs.translation: 根据心理学家萨比娜·里德的说法，当成年子女共享家庭住所时，可能会有一些非常积极的结果，并指出“亲子关系可能在这个过程中确实得到加强和成熟”。

paragraphs.text: But, she notes, a strong __33__ doesn't simply come with time. "The many changing factors of the relationship need to be acknowledged, rather than hoping that the mere passage of time will __34__ connect parents to their adult children. It's important to acknowledge that the relationship parameters have changed to avoid falling back into __35__ from the teen years."
paragraphs.translation: 但是，她指出，牢固的纽带并不会随着时间的推移自然形成。“关系的许多变化因素需要被承认，而不是希望时间的流逝会神奇地将父母与成年子女连接起来。重要的是要承认关系的参数已经改变，以避免退回到青少年时期的模式。”

questionGroups.title: How Telemedicine Is Transforming Healthcare

paragraphs.text: After years of big promises, telemedicine is finally living up to its potential. Driven by faster internet connections, ubiquitous (无处不在的) smartphones and changing insurance standards, more health providers are turning to electronic communications to do their jobs--and it's dramatically changing the delivery of healthcare.
paragraphs.translation: 经过多年的大肆宣传，远程医疗终于开始发挥其潜力。在更快的互联网连接、无处不在的智能手机和不断变化的保险标准的推动下，越来越多的医疗提供者转向电子通信来开展工作——这正在极大地改变医疗服务的交付方式。

paragraphs.text: Doctors are linking up with patients by phone, email and webcam (网络摄像头). They're also consulting with each other electronically -- sometimes to make split-second decisions on heart attacks and strokes. Patients, meanwhile, are using new devices to relay their blood pressure, heart rate and other vital signs to their doctors so they can manage chronic conditions at home. Telemedicine also allows for better care in places where medical expertise is hard to come by. Five to 10 times a day, Doctors Without Borders relays questions about tough cases from its physicians in Niger, South Sudan and elsewhere to its network of 280 experts around the world, and back again via the internet.
paragraphs.translation: 医生通过电话、电子邮件和网络摄像头与患者联系。他们也通过电子方式相互咨询——有时是为了在心脏病发作和中风问题上做出瞬息之间的决定。与此同时，患者使用新设备将他们的血压、心率和其他生命体征传送给医生，以便他们在家管理慢性疾病。远程医疗还允许在医疗专业知识难以获得的地方提供更好的护理。每天五到十次，无国界医生将其在尼日利亚、南苏丹等地的医生关于疑难病例的问题转发给其全球280位专家网络，并通过互联网传回。

paragraphs.text: As a measure of how rapidly telemedicine is spreading, consider: More than 15 million Americans received some kind of medical care remotely last year, according to the American Telemedicine Association, a trade group, which expects those numbers to grow by 30% this year.
paragraphs.translation: 作为衡量远程医疗传播速度的一个指标，考虑一下：根据美国远程医疗协会（一个贸易团体）的数据，去年有超过1500万美国人接受了某种远程医疗服务，该协会预计今年这些数字将增长30%。

paragraphs.text: None of this is to say that telemedicine has found its way into all corners of medicine. A recent survey of 500 tech-savvy (精通技术的) consumers found that 39% hadn't heard of telemedicine, and of those who haven't used it, 42% said they preferred in-person doctor visits. In a poll of 1 500 family physicians, only 15% had used it in their practices but 90% said they would if it were appropriately reimbursed (补偿).
paragraphs.translation: 这并不是说远程医疗已经渗透到医学的各个角落。最近对500名精通技术的消费者进行的一项调查发现，39%的人没有听说过远程医疗，而在那些没有使用过的人中，42%表示他们更喜欢面对面的医生访问。在一项对1500名家庭医生的民意调查中，只有15%在他们的实践中使用过它，但90%表示如果得到适当的补偿，他们会使用。

paragraphs.text: What's more, for all the rapid growth, significant questions and challenges remain. Rules defining and regulating telemedicine differ widely from state to state. Physicians groups are issuing different guidelines about what care they consider appropriate to deliver and in what form.
paragraphs.translation: 此外，尽管增长迅速，但重大的问题和挑战仍然存在。定义和监管远程医疗的规则因州而异。医生团体正在发布不同的指南，关于他们认为适合以何种形式提供何种护理。

paragraphs.text: Some critics also question whether the quality of care is keeping up with the rapid expansion of telemedicine. And there's the question of what services physicians should be paid for: Insurance coverage varies from health plan to health plan, and a big federal plan covers only a narrow range of services. Telemedicine's future will depend on how and whether regulators, providers, payers and patients can address these challenges. Here's a closer look at some of these issues:
paragraphs.translation: 一些批评者还质疑护理质量是否跟上了远程医疗的快速扩张。还有一个问题是医生应该为哪些服务获得报酬：保险覆盖范围因健康计划而异，一个大型联邦计划只覆盖有限的服务范围。远程医疗的未来将取决于监管机构、提供者、支付者和患者如何以及是否能够应对这些挑战。以下是对其中一些问题的更仔细审视：

paragraphs.text: Do patients trade quality for convenience? The fastest-growing services in telemedicine connect consumers with clinicians they've never met for a phone, video or email visit-on-demand, 24/7. Typically, these are for nonemergency issues such as colds, flu, ear-aches and skin rashes, and they cost around $45, compared with approximately $100 at a doctor's office, $160 at an urgent care clinic or $750 and up at an emergency room.
paragraphs.translation: 患者是否以质量换取便利？远程医疗中增长最快的服务将消费者与他们从未见过的临床医生连接起来，进行电话、视频或电子邮件访问，全天候按需服务。通常，这些服务用于非紧急问题，如感冒、流感、耳朵痛和皮疹，费用约为45美元，相比之下，在医生办公室约100美元，在紧急护理诊所约160美元，在急诊室750美元以上。

paragraphs.text: Many health plans and employers have rushed to offer the services and promote them as a convenient way for plan members to get medical care without leaving home or work. Nearly three quarters of large employers will offer virtual doctor visits as a benefit to employees this year, up from 48% last year. Web companies such as Teladoc and American Well are expected to host some 1.2 million such virtual doctor visits this year, up 20% from last year, according to the American Telemedicine Association.
paragraphs.translation: 许多健康计划和雇主急于提供这些服务，并将它们宣传为计划成员无需离开家或工作即可获得医疗保健的便捷方式。今年，近四分之三的大型雇主将提供虚拟医生访问作为员工福利，高于去年的48%。根据美国远程医疗协会的数据，Teladoc和American Well等网络公司预计今年将举办约120万次此类虚拟医生访问，比去年增长20%。

paragraphs.text: But critics worry that such services may be sacrificing quality for convenience. Consulting a random doctor patients will never meet, they say, further fragments the health-care system, and even minor issues such as upper respiratory (上呼吸道的) infections can't be thoroughly evaluated by a doctor who can't listen to your heart or feel your swollen glands. In a recent study, researchers posing as patients with skin problems sought help from 16 telemedicine sites with unsettling results. In 62 encounters, fewer than one-third disclosed clinicians' credentials or let patients choose; only 32% discussed potential side effects of prescribed medications. Several sites misdiagnosed serious conditions, largely because they failed to ask basic follow-up questions, the researchers said. "Telemedicine holds enormous promise, but these sites are just not ready for prime time, " says Jack Resneck, the study's lead author.
paragraphs.translation: 但批评者担心，此类服务可能以牺牲质量换取便利。他们说，咨询患者永远不会再见到的随机医生，进一步使医疗保健系统碎片化，即使是上呼吸道感染等小问题，也无法由无法听心脏或触摸肿胀腺体的医生彻底评估。在最近的一项研究中，研究人员假扮有皮肤问题的患者向16个远程医疗网站寻求帮助，结果令人不安。在62次接触中，只有不到三分之一披露了临床医生的资质或让患者选择；只有32%讨论了处方药的潜在副作用。研究人员说，几个网站误诊了严重疾病，主要是因为他们没有提出基本的后续问题。杰克·雷斯尼克，该研究的首席作者，说：“远程医疗前景巨大，但这些网站尚未准备好迎接黄金时代。”

paragraphs.text: The American Telemedicine Association and other organizations have started accreditation (鉴定) programs to identify top-quality telemedicine sites. The American Medical Association this month approved new ethical guidelines for telemedicine, calling for participating doctors to recognize the limitations of such services and ensure that they have sufficient information to make clinical recommendations.
paragraphs.translation: 美国远程医疗协会和其他组织已经启动了鉴定计划，以识别高质量的远程医疗网站。美国医学会本月批准了远程医疗的新伦理指南，呼吁参与的医生认识到此类服务的局限性，并确保他们有足够的信息来提出临床建议。

paragraphs.text: Who pays for the services? While employers and health plans have been eager to cover virtual urgent care visits, insurers have been far less willing to pay for telemedicine when doctors use phone, email or video to consult with existing patients about continuing issues. "It's very hard to get paid unless you physically see the patient," says Peter Rasmussen, medical director of distance health at the Cleveland Clinic. Some 32 states have passed "parity" (等同的) laws requiring private insurers to reimburse doctors for services delivered remotely if the same service would be covered in person, though not necessarily at the same rate or frequency. Medicare lags further behind. The federal health plan for the elderly covers a small number of telemedicine services only for beneficiaries in rural areas and only when the services are received in a hospital, doctor's office or clinic.
paragraphs.translation: 谁为这些服务付费？虽然雇主和健康计划一直急于覆盖虚拟紧急护理访问，但当医生使用电话、电子邮件或视频咨询现有患者关于持续问题时，保险公司远不愿意为远程医疗付费。克利夫兰诊所远程健康医疗主任彼得·拉斯穆森说：“除非你亲自见到患者，否则很难获得报酬。”大约32个州通过了“等同”法律，要求私人保险公司报销远程提供的服务，如果相同服务在面对面时会被覆盖，但不一定以相同的速率或频率。医疗保险进一步落后。针对老年人的联邦健康计划只覆盖少数远程医疗服务，仅限于农村地区的受益人，并且只有当服务在医院、医生办公室或诊所接受时。

paragraphs.text: Bills to expand Medicare coverage of telemedicine have bipartisan (两党的) support in Congress. Opponents worry that such expansion would be costly for taxpayers, but advocates say it would save money in the long run.
paragraphs.translation: 扩大医疗保险覆盖远程医疗的法案在国会得到了两党的支持。反对者担心这种扩大会对纳税人来说成本高昂，但倡导者说从长远来看会节省资金。

paragraphs.text: Experts say more hospitals are likely to invest in telemedicine systems as they move away from fee for-service payments and into managed-care-type contracts that give them a set fee to provide care for patients and allow them to keep any savings they achieve.
paragraphs.translation: 专家表示，随着医院从按服务收费转向托管式合同，为提供患者护理支付固定费用并允许它们保留所实现的任何节省，更多的医院可能会投资远程医疗系统。

paragraphs.text: Is the state-by-state regulatory system outdated? Historically, regulation of medicine has been left to individual states. But some industry members contend that having 50 different sets of rules, licensing fees and even definitions of "medical practice" makes less sense in the era of telemedicine and is hampering its growth. Currently, doctors must have a valid license in the state where the patient is located to provide medical care, which means virtual-visit companies can match users only with locally licensed clinicians. It also causes administrative hassles (麻烦) for world-class medical centers that attract patients from across the country. At the Mayo Clinic, doctors who treat out-of-state patients can follow up with them via phone, email or web chats when they return home, but they can only discuss the conditions they treated in person. "If the patient wants to talk about a new problem, the doctor has to be licensed in that state to discuss it. If not, the patient should talk to his primary-care physician about it, " says Steve Ommen, who runs Mayo's Connected Care program.
paragraphs.translation: 逐州监管系统是否过时？历史上，医学的监管留给了各个州。但一些行业成员认为，在远程医疗时代，拥有50套不同的规则、许可费甚至“医疗实践”的定义意义不大，并阻碍了其发展。目前，医生必须在患者所在州拥有有效的执照才能提供医疗服务，这意味着虚拟访问公司只能将用户与本地许可的临床医生匹配。这也为吸引全国各地患者的世界级医疗中心带来了行政麻烦。在梅奥诊所，治疗州外患者的医生可以在患者回家后通过电话、电子邮件或网络聊天与他们跟进，但只能讨论他们亲自治疗的疾病。史蒂夫·奥门，运营梅奥的Connected Care计划，说：“如果患者想讨论一个新问题，医生必须在该州获得许可才能讨论。如果没有，患者应该与他的初级保健医生讨论。”

paragraphs.text: To date, 17 states have joined a compact that will allow a doctor licensed in one member state to quickly obtain a license in another. While welcoming the move, some telemedicine advocates would prefer states to automatically honor one another's licenses, as they do with drivers' licenses. But states aren't likely to surrender control of medical practice, and most are considering new regulations. This year, more than 200 telemedicine-related bills have been introduced in 42 states, many regarding what services Medicaid will cover and whether payers should reimburse for remote patient monitoring. "A lot of states are still trying to define telemedicine, " says Lisa Robbin, chief advocacy officer for the Federation of State Medical Boards.
paragraphs.translation: 迄今为止，已有17个州加入了一项协议，允许在一个成员州获得许可的医生快速在另一个州获得许可。虽然欢迎这一举措，但一些远程医疗倡导者希望各州自动互相承认执照，就像他们对驾驶执照所做的那样。但各州不太可能放弃对医疗实践的控制，大多数正在考虑新的法规。今年，42个州引入了200多项与远程医疗相关的法案，许多关于医疗补助将覆盖哪些服务以及支付者是否应该报销远程患者监测。丽莎·罗宾，州医学委员会联合会的首席倡导官，说：“许多州仍在试图定义远程医疗。”

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Danielle Steel, the 71-year-old romance novelist is notoriously productive, having published 179 books at a rate of up to seven a year. But a passing reference in a recent profile by Glamour magazine to her 20-hour workdays prompted an outpouring of admiration.
paragraphs.translation: 丹妮尔·斯蒂尔，这位71岁的言情小说家以其高产出而闻名，已出版179本书，年产量高达七本。但《魅力》杂志最近的一篇人物简介中偶然提及她每天工作20小时，这引发了人们的一片钦佩之情。

paragraphs.text: Steel has given that 20-hour figure when describing her "exhausting" process in the past: "I start the book and don't leave my desk until the first draft is finished. " She goes from bed, to desk, to bath, to bed, avoiding all contact aside from phone calls with her nine children. "I don't comb my hair for weeks, " she says. Meals are brought to her desk, where she types until her fingers swell and her nails bleed.
paragraphs.translation: 斯蒂尔过去在描述她“筋疲力尽”的创作过程时曾提到那个20小时的数字：“我开始写书，直到完成初稿才离开书桌。”她从床到书桌，到浴室，再回到床，除了与九个孩子通电话外，避免一切接触。“我几周不梳头，”她说。饭菜被送到她的书桌前，她在那里打字，直到手指肿胀、指甲流血。

paragraphs.text: The business news website Quartz held Steel up as an inspiration, writing that if only we all followed her "actually extremely liberating" example of industrious sleeplessness, we would be quick to see results.
paragraphs.translation: 商业新闻网站Quartz将斯蒂尔视为灵感来源，写道如果我们都能效仿她“实际上极其解放”的勤奋不眠榜样，我们很快就会看到成果。

paragraphs.text: Well, indeed. With research results showing the cumulative effects of sleep loss and its impact on productivity, doubt has been voiced about the accuracy of Steel's self-assessment. Her output may be undeniable, but sceptics have suggested that she is guilty of erasing the role of ghostwriters (代笔人) at worst, gross exaggeration at best.
paragraphs.translation: 确实如此。随着研究结果显示睡眠不足的累积效应及其对生产力的影响，人们对斯蒂尔自我评估的准确性产生了怀疑。她的产出或许不可否认，但怀疑者认为，她最坏的情况是抹杀了代笔人的作用，最好的情况也是严重夸大。

paragraphs.text: Steel says working 20 hours a day is "pretty brutal physically. " But is it even possible? "No," says Maryanne Taylor of the Sleep Works. While you could work that long, the impact on productivity would make it hardly worthwhile. If Steel was routinely sleeping for four hours a night, she would be drastically underestimating the negative impact, says Alison Gardiner, founder of the sleep improvement programme Sleepstation. "It's akin to being drunk. "
paragraphs.translation: 斯蒂尔说每天工作20小时“在身体上相当残酷”。但这可能吗？“不可能，”Sleep Works的玛丽安·泰勒说。虽然你可以工作那么长时间，但对生产力的影响会使其几乎不值得。如果斯蒂尔通常每晚只睡四小时，她就会严重低估负面影响，睡眠改善项目Sleepstation的创始人艾莉森·加德纳说。“这就像喝醉了一样。

paragraphs.text: It's possible that Steel is exaggerating the demands of her schedule. Self-imposed sleeplessness has "become a bit of a status symbol", says Taylor, a misguided measure to prove how powerful and productive you are. Margaret Thatcher was also said to get by on four hours a night, while the 130-hour work weeks endured by tech heads has been held up as key to their success.
paragraphs.translation: 斯蒂尔可能夸大了她的日程需求。泰勒说，自我强加的睡眠不足“已经成为一种地位象征”，这是一种误导性的衡量标准，用来证明你有多强大和多产。据说玛格丽特·撒切尔每晚也只睡四小时，而科技巨头们忍受的每周130小时工作时间被奉为他们成功的关键。

paragraphs.text: That is starting to change with increased awareness of the importance of sleep for mental health. "People are starting to realise that sleep should not be something that you fit in between everything else," says Taylor.
paragraphs.translation: 随着人们对睡眠对心理健康重要性的认识增加，这正在改变。“人们开始意识到，睡眠不应该是在其他所有事情之间见缝插针的东西，”泰勒说。

paragraphs.text: But it is possible—if statistically extremely unlikely-that Steel could be born a "short sleeper" with an unusual body clock, says sleep expert Dr. Sophie Bostock. "It's probably present in fewer than 1% of the population. "
paragraphs.translation: 但睡眠专家索菲·博斯托克博士说，斯蒂尔可能天生就是“短睡眠者”，拥有不寻常的生物钟，尽管从统计上看极不可能。“这可能存在于不到1%的人口中。

paragraphs.text: Even if Steel does happen to be among that tiny minority, says Bostock, it's "pretty irresponsible" to suggest that 20-hour days are simply a question of discipline for the rest of us.
paragraphs.translation: 博斯托克说，即使斯蒂尔恰好属于那极少数人，认为对我们其他人来说每天20小时工作只是纪律问题，也是“相当不负责任的”。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Organic agriculture is a relatively untapped resource for feeding the Earth's population, especially in the face of climate change and other global challenges. That's the conclusion I reached in reviewing 40 years of science comparing the long-term prospects of organic and conventional farming.
paragraphs.translation: 有机农业是养活地球人口的一种相对未开发的资源，尤其是在面对气候变化和其他全球挑战时。这是我在回顾比较有机和常规农业长期前景的40年科学研究后得出的结论。

paragraphs.text: The review study, "Organic Agriculture in the 21st Century, " is featured as the cover story for the February issue of the journal Nature Plants. It is the first to compare organic and conventional agriculture across the main goals of sustainability identified by the National Academy of Sciences: productivity, economics, and environment.
paragraphs.translation: 这项题为“21世纪的有机农业”的综述研究是《自然·植物》杂志二月刊的封面故事。它是首次在国家科学院确定的可持续性主要目标（生产率、经济效益和环境）方面比较有机和常规农业。

paragraphs.text: Critics have long argued that organic agriculture is inefficient, requiring more land to yield the same amount of food. It's true that organic farming produces lower yields, averaging 10 to 20 percent less than conventional. Advocates contend that the environmental advantages of organic agriculture far outweigh the lower yields, and that increasing research and breeding resources for organic systems would reduce the yield gap. Sometimes excluded from these arguments is the fact that we already produce enough food to more than feed the world's 7.4 billion people but do not provide adequate access to all individuals.
paragraphs.translation: 批评者长期以来认为有机农业效率低下，需要更多土地才能产出同等数量的食物。确实，有机农业产量较低，平均比常规农业低10%到20%。支持者认为，有机农业的环境优势远超过其较低的产量，并且增加对有机系统的研发和育种资源将缩小产量差距。有时这些争论中忽略了一个事实：我们已经生产了足以养活全球74亿人口的食物，但并非所有人都能充分获取。

paragraphs.text: In some cases, organic yields can be higher than conventional. For example, in severe drought conditions, which are expected to increase with climate change in many areas, organic farms can produce as good, if not better, yields because of the higher water-holding capacity of organically farmed soils.
paragraphs.translation: 在某些情况下，有机产量可能高于常规。例如，在严重干旱条件下（预计气候变化将导致许多地区干旱加剧），由于有机耕作土壤具有更高的持水能力，有机农场可以产出同样好甚至更好的产量。

paragraphs.text: What science does tell us is that mainstream conventional farming systems have provided growing supplies of food and other products but often at the expense of other sustainability goals.
paragraphs.translation: 科学告诉我们的是，主流常规农业系统虽然提供了不断增长的食品和其他产品供应，但往往是以牺牲其他可持续性目标为代价。

paragraphs.text: Conventional agriculture may produce more food, but it often comes at a cost to the environment. Biodiversity loss, environmental degradation, and severe impacts on ecosystem services have not only accompanied conventional farming systems but have often extended well beyond their field boundaries. With organic agriculture, environmental costs tend to be lower and the benefits greater.
paragraphs.translation: 常规农业可能生产更多食物，但往往以环境为代价。生物多样性丧失、环境退化以及对生态系统的严重影响，不仅伴随常规农业系统，而且常常延伸到农田边界之外。对于有机农业，环境成本往往更低，而收益更大。

paragraphs.text: Overall, organic farms tend to store more soil carbon, have better soil quality, and reduce soil erosion compared to their conventional counterparts. Organic agriculture also creates less soil and water pollution and lower greenhouse gas emissions. And it's more energy-efficient because it doesn't rely on synthetic fertilizers or pesticides.
paragraphs.translation: 总体而言，与常规农场相比，有机农场倾向于储存更多土壤碳，拥有更好的土壤质量，并减少土壤侵蚀。有机农业还造成更少的土壤和水污染，以及更低的温室气体排放。而且它更节能，因为它不依赖合成肥料或农药。

paragraphs.text: Organic agriculture is also associated with greater biodiversity of plants, animals, insects and microorganisms as well as genetic diversity. Biodiversity increases the services that nature provides and improves the ability of farming systems to adapt to changing conditions.
paragraphs.translation: 有机农业还与植物、动物、昆虫和微生物的更大生物多样性以及遗传多样性相关。生物多样性增加了自然提供的服务，并提高了农业系统适应变化条件的能力。

paragraphs.text: Despite lower yields, organic agriculture is more profitable for farmers because consumers are willing to pay more. Higher prices, called price premiums, can be justified as a way to compensate farmers for providing ecosystem services and avoiding environmental damage or external costs.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管产量较低，有机农业对农民来说更有利可图，因为消费者愿意支付更高的价格。更高的价格，称为价格溢价，可以作为一种补偿方式，以奖励农民提供生态系统服务和避免环境损害或外部成本。

options.text: The long-term prospects of organic farming are yet to be explored.

options.label: D
options.text: Organic farming is at least as promising as conventional farming.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第一段提到作者得出的结论是'Organic agriculture is a relatively untapped resource for feeding the Earth's population'，说明有机农业是一个未被充分利用的资源，可以用来解决全球粮食问题。因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有提到需要开发更多资源来养活世界人口，而是强调有机农业是一个未被充分利用的资源。
wrongOptions.C: 原文第一段已经得出结论，说明有机农业的长期前景已经被探索。
wrongOptions.D: 原文没有将有机农业和传统农业进行直接比较，而是强调有机农业是一个未被充分利用的资源。

questions.questionText: What is the critics' argument against organic farming?

options.label: A
options.text: It cannot meet the need for food.

options.label: B
options.text: It cannot increase farm yields.

options.label: C
options.text: It is not really practical.

options.label: D
options.text: It is not that productive.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到批评者认为有机农业效率低下，需要更多的土地来生产同样数量的食物，说明有机农业的生产力不如传统农业。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 批评者并没有说有机农业不能满足食物需求，而是说它效率低下。
wrongOptions.B: 批评者并没有说有机农业不能增加农场产量，而是说它效率低下。
wrongOptions.C: 批评者并没有说有机农业不切实际，而是说它效率低下。

questions.questionText: What does the author think should be taken into account in arguing about organic farming?

options.label: A
options.text: Growth in world population.

options.label: B
options.text: Deterioration in soil fertility.

options.label: C
options.text: Inequality in food distribution.

options.label: D
options.text: Advance in farming technology.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第四段提到'Sometimes excluded from these arguments is the fact that we already produce enough food to more than feed the world's 7.4 billion people but do not provide adequate access to all individuals'，说明在讨论有机农业时应该考虑食物分配不均的问题。因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有提到世界人口增长的问题。
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有提到土壤肥力恶化的问题。
wrongOptions.D: 原文没有提到农业技术进步的问题。

questions.questionText: What does science tell us about conventional farming?

options.label: A
options.text: It will not be able to meet global food demand.

options.label: B
options.text: It is not conducive to sustainable development.

options.label: C
options.text: It will eventually give way to organic farming.

options.label: D
options.text: It is going mainstream throughout the world.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章倒数第二段提到传统农业虽然可以生产更多食物，但往往以牺牲其他可持续性目标为代价，如生物多样性丧失、环境退化等。说明传统农业不利于可持续发展。因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有说传统农业不能满足全球粮食需求。
wrongOptions.C: 原文没有说传统农业最终会被有机农业取代。
wrongOptions.D: 原文没有说传统农业正在全球范围内成为主流。

questions.questionText: Why does the author think higher prices of organic farm produce are justifiable?

options.label: A
options.text: They give farmers going organic a big competitive edge.

options.label: B
options.text: They motivate farmers to upgrade farming technology.

options.label: C
options.text: Organic farming costs more than conventional farming.

options.label: D
options.text: Organic farming does long-term good to the ecosystem.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到有机农业对生态系统长期有益，因此消费者愿意支付更高的价格，作为对农民提供生态系统服务和避免环境损害的补偿。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有说有机农业产品价格高可以给农民带来竞争优势。
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有说有机农业产品价格高可以激励农民升级农业技术。
wrongOptions.C: 原文没有说有机农业成本高于传统农业。

《水浒传》(Water Margin)是中国文学四大经典小说之一。这部小说基于历史人物宋江及其伙伴反抗封建帝王的故事，数百年来一直深受中国读者的喜爱。
毫不夸张地说，几乎每个中国人都熟悉小说中的一些主要人物。这部小说中的精彩故事在茶馆、戏剧舞台、广播电视、电影屏幕和无数家庭中反复讲述。事实上，这部小说的影响已经远远超出了国界。越来越多的外国读者也感到这部小说里的故事生动感人、趣味盎然。

answer.modelTranslation: Water Margin is one of the four great classic novels of Chinese literature. This novel, based on the historical figures Song Jiang and his companions' resistance against the feudal emperor, has been beloved by Chinese readers for centuries. It is no exaggeration to say that almost every Chinese person is familiar with some of the main characters in the novel. The exciting stories in this novel have been repeatedly told in tea houses, on theatrical stages, through radio and television, on movie screens, and in countless homes. In fact, the influence of this novel has far exceeded national boundaries. An increasing number of foreign readers also find the stories in this novel vivid, touching, and interesting.
translationNotes: 注意'四大经典小说之一'的翻译，使用'one of the four great classic novels'

'数百年来'译为'for centuries'，注意时态使用现在完成时
'毫不夸张地说'可以翻译为'It is no exaggeration to say'
'深受...喜爱'译为'has been beloved by'
'熟悉'译为'familiar with'，注意使用现在分词形式
'反复讲述'译为'have been repeatedly told'，注意时态和语态的使用
'远远超出了国界'译为'far exceeded national boundaries'，注意使用现在完成时
'生动感人、趣味盎然'可以翻译为'vivid, touching, and interesting'
